_why: Written 2026-08-08. Nightshelf bundles its whole library but also calls storyvault-api for custom AI stories and cloud narration, so 'works offline' is true of THE SHELF and false of the AI features. Every approval below is worded around that split. Verified against /Users/dee/Developer/DrVanus/Nightshelf.

evidence: There is no sign-in surface: a grep of Nightshelf for ASAuthorization, SignInWithApple, GIDSignIn and signIn( returns nothing, and there is no account, profile or password screen in the app.
privacy.html states it as 'There is no account, no sign-in, no analytics SDK, no third-party tracker, and no advertising', which matches the code exactly.
Nightshelf Pro is a StoreKit subscription; it unlocks books without introducing an identity.

No analytics, attribution or crash SDK is linked: a grep of the Nightshelf xcodeproj project.pbxproj for GoogleMobileAds, AdMob, PostHog, Mixpanel, Amplitude, Crashlytics and FirebaseAnalytics returns nothing, and no such import appears in any *.swift.

SCOPE — the backend keeps a counter-style log, and the site discloses it rather than denying it: the streaming route the shipping app hits (storyvault-api routes.py:801) records setting, tone, target_minutes, has_prompt_hint and chapters. No title, story text or prompt_hint is logged (commit 42ab9a6); there is no story table; rows are pruned at 35 days. Do not widen this claim into 'we log nothing'.
No advertising SDK is linked (same project.pbxproj grep as no_tracking) and there is no ad placement anywhere in the app.

The free tier is funded by the Pro subscription, not by advertising: index.html's 'No account. No ads. Just goodnights.' and support.html's 'they stay free ... with no account and no ads' both describe the thirteen free books.
There is no account, no form and no contact field in the app, so no name, email or address is ever collected.

Reading progress and settings stay on the device. What DOES leave on a custom-story request is the story parameters — setting, tone, weather, time_of_night and length (Nightshelf/.../CustomStoryGenerator.swift:110) — which privacy.html enumerates in its 'what leaves your device' bullet. None of it identifies a person.

SCOPED TO THE SHELF, which is how both pages word it: 'All 82 books are installed with the app, so the shelf works offline' (terms.html) and 'all eighty-two are installed either way — that is why the shelf works offline' (support.html).
Verified by count: Nightshelf/Nightshelf/Nightshelf/Resources/Books contains exactly 82 .txt files, bundled into the app. A locked book shows a padlock rather than requiring a download.

THE AI FEATURES ARE NOT OFFLINE — CustomStoryCoverGenerator.swift:102 and NightshelfVoices.swift:657 both call URLSession against storyvault-api. No page claims otherwise; keep the word 'shelf' in the sentence.
